{{Current events|year=2020|month=08|day=21|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**Chief of the [[Government of National Accord]] (GNA) [[Fayez al-Sarraj]] orders a [[ceasefire]] in all the territory of [[Libya]]. The statement ordered "to all military forces to immediately ceasefire and all combat operations in all Libyan territories". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/libyas-tripoli-based-government-declares-ceasefire-statement-idUSKBN25H1BG (Reuters)]
**GNA's rival leader of the eastern-based front [[Aguila Saleh Issa]] appeals to a halt of hostilities from both sides and supports the ceasefire to fight the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Libya]]. There has been no comment from [[Libyan National Army]] (LNA) leader [[Khalifa Haftar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/libyas-tripoli-based-government-and-a-rival-parliament-take-steps-to-end-hostilities-idUSKBN25H1BG?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Three people, including two policemen and the mayor's son, are killed by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]-linked militants attack a Christian village in [[Kaftoun]], [[Lebanon]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-08/24/c_139314550.htm (Xinhua)]

;Arts and culture
* The official music video for [[BTS]]' [[Dynamite (BTS song)|Dynamite]] breaks the all-time record on [[YouTube]] for the [[List_of_most-viewed_online_videos_in_the_first_24_hours|highest number of views on a single video in 24 hours]], generating 101,100,000 views in its first 24 hours. [https://www.nydailynews.com/snyde/ny-kpop-bts-video-dynamite-youtube-record-most-views-24-hours-20200823-xe6b54mbhfcwxpk2i2zvjis3pi-story.html (''NY Daily News'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Vice-Chancellor of Germany|Vice Chancellor]] and [[Federal Ministry of Finance (Germany)|Federal Finance Minister]] [[Olaf Scholz]] announces a plan to loan around [[Euro|€]]218 billion ([[United States dollar|$]]258bn) for a [[bailout]] to mitigate the impact of the country's recession caused by the pandemic, thereby suspending the [[Debt brake (Germany)|debt brake]]. [https://news.cgtn.com/news/2020-08-21/Germany-to-take-on-more-debt-in-2021-due-to-virus-finance-minister-T7ZkIVRfR6/index.html (CGTN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom national debt|UK's national debt]] exceeds [[Pound sterling|£]]2 trillion ([[United States dollar|$]]2.61tn) for the first time, according to data from the [[Office for National Statistics]]. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2020/08/618277/uk-government-debt-exceeds-%C2%A32-trillion-first-time (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****The [[Singapore]]an [[Ministry of Health (Singapore)|Ministry of Health]] announces that it would permit the entry of travelers from [[Brunei]] and [[New Zealand]], effective September 1, citing the countries' effective responses to pandemic. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/08/21/singapore-to-allow-new-zealand-brunei-visitors-in-first-border-easing.html (Reuters via CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon]], [[Lebanese liquidity crisis]]
***The [[S&P Global Ratings]] downgrades [[Lebanon]]'s credit rating for its [[external debt]] to "selective default" (SD), following [[Default (finance)|defaults]] due to the resignation of the [[Government of Lebanon|government]] in the aftermath of the [[2020 Beirut explosion|August 4 explosion]] in [[Beirut]] and the implementation of a two-week lockdown from August 18 following a surge in infections. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200821-s-p-downgrades-lebanon-bonds-to-default-after-missed-payments (AFP via France 24)]
**State-run oil company [[Saudi Aramco]] suspends plans to build a [[United States dollar|US$]]10 billion [[oil refinery]] in [[Liaoning]], [[China]], due to decreased global demand for oil. Its Chinese partners said they will press ahead with the project. [https://www.aljazeera.com/ajimpact/saudi-aramco-puts-10bn-china-oil-refinery-deal-ice-200821124235907.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announced that the [[drilling ship]] ''[[Fatih (drillship)|Fatih]]'' has found 320 billion cubic meters of [[natural gas reserves]] in the [[Black Sea]], [[Turkey]]'s biggest [[natural gas]] find to date. If Turkey can extract the gas commercially, it will be able to reduce its reliance on imported energy. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-53866217 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**[[August 2020 California lightning wildfires]]
***Structures at the [[Big Basin Redwoods State Park]] are damaged or destroyed by the [[CZU Lightning Complex Fire]] in [[Santa Cruz County, California|Santa Cruz County]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/21/us/ca-oldest-state-park-damaged-wildfires-trnd/index.html (CNN)]
***Six people die in the wildfires in [[Northern California]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/dead-massive-california-wildfire-community-turns-volunteer-firefighters/story?id=72524560 (ABC News)]
***The [[LNU Lightning Complex Fire]] grows to 220,000 acres, with 7% of the fire contained. [https://www.sfgate.com/news/bayarea/article/Lnu-Complex-Fire-Grows-To-Nearly-220-000-Acres-By-15504767.php (SFGate)] 

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Chief Executive of Hong Kong|Chief Executive]] [[Carrie Lam]] announces mass COVID-19 testing for residents starting on September 1, with the assistance of a 60-person team from the [[mainland China|mainland]], which is the first time Chinese health officials have assisted the [[Special administrative regions of China|special administrative region]] in its battle to control the epidemic. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-hong-kong-mass-testing-sep-carrie-lam-coronavirus-13041434 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****Israel surpasses 100,000 cases as the government struggles with a resurgence of infections. The death tally stands at 809. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/08/21/Coronavirus-Israel-hits-100-000-COVID-19-cases-amid-criticism-of-gov-t-response.html (Al Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****The [[Rakhine State Government|state government]] of [[Rakhine State|Rakhine]] imposes a night-time curfew in the state's capital of [[Sittwe]], after the [[Ministry of Health and Sports (Myanmar)|Ministry of Health and Sports]] reported a surge in local cases. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/myanmar-imposes-curfew-on-rakhine-state-capital/1948939 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports 324 new cases in the previous 24 hours. This is the highest number of new cases since March 8, as the authorities warn of a cluster of infections in [[Seoul]] threatening to spread nationwide. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-southkorea/south-korea-urges-more-testing-quarantines-as-coronavirus-outbreak-threatens-to-spread-idUSKBN25H06Z (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****The opposition-controlled region of the northwest of [[Syria]] reports its first death from COVID-19, that of an 80-year-old woman who suffered from severe renal insufficiency and high blood pressure. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/08/21/Coronavirus-Northwest-Syria-records-first-COVID-19-death.html (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****At least 41 schools in [[Berlin]] have reported students or teachers are infected with COVID-19 less than two weeks after they reopened. Hundreds of students and teachers are in quarantine and Elementary schools, high schools and trade schools are affected. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/virus-schools-berlin-1.5694994 (AP via CBC News)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Prime Minister of Hungary|Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] announces on state radio that he will tighten border crossing rules in [[Hungary]] on September 1 to prevent the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] as the number of new infections rises in neighbouring countries. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hungary-economy/hungary-to-tighten-border-crossing-as-of-sept-1-to-curb-spread-of-coronavirus-pm-orban-idUSKBN25H0IU (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reports 947 new cases, touching the same levels recorded in mid-May, when the government started easing its stringent lockdown measures. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/italy-records-new-surge-in-daily-coronavirus-cases/1949503 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire]]
****[[Governor of New Hampshire|New Hampshire Governor]] [[Chris Sununu]] announces that restaurants in the state can now open at 100% dine-in capacity. [https://www.newsweek.com/new-hampshires-gop-governor-allows-restaurants-open-100-capacity-1526890 (''Newsweek'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***American company [[Pfizer]] and German company [[BioNTech]] say that they are on track to being submitted for regulatory review as early as October. [https://www.financialexpress.com/lifestyle/health/pfizer-vaccine-on-track-for-regulatory-review-in-october/2061627/ (''Financial Express'')]

;International relations
*[[Mali–United States relations]]
**The U.S. announces through its Sahel Region representative [[J. Peter Pham]] that it is halting military cooperation with [[Mali]] over the [[2020 Malian coup d'état|recent coup]] until the recent situation is "clarified". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/u-s-halts-military-cooperation-with-mali-as-coup-supporters-celebrate-idUSKBN25H190?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**A U.S. attempt to extend [[Sanctions against Iran#UN sanctions against Iran|United Nations sanctions against Iran]] under a [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|JCPoA]] "snapback" provision is opposed by 13 [[United Nations Security Council|Security Council]] members, who argue that the U.S. [[United States withdrawal from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|left]] the agreement with [[Iran]] in 2018. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/21/us-iran-sanctions-un-mike-pompeo (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan relations]]
**The [[Pakistan]]i Foreign Ministry reveals that it on August 18 placed financial sanctions on dozens of [[Taliban]] members, including chief negotiator [[Abdul Ghani Baradar|Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar]], and deputy head and [[Haqqani network]] leader [[Sirajuddin Haqqani]]. The sanctions were placed to avoid placing the country on the [[Financial Action Task Force]] blacklist. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/pakistan-sanctions-taliban-avoid-global-finance-blacklist-200822151917665.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*A court in [[Zimbabwe]] denies, for the third time, bail to opposition politician and activist Jacob Ngarivhume after ruling he "could be a danger to the public if released", over protests he organized last month. His lawyer says he is "stunned" by the court's decision. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-zimbabwe-protests/zimbabwe-politician-who-called-for-protests-denied-bail-for-third-time-idUSKBN25H1IQ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Salman of Saudi Arabia|King Salman]] of [[Saudi Arabia]] dismisses [[Awwad Eid Al-Aradi Al-Balawi]], the [[General Directorate of Border Guard|directorate general of the Border Guards]], and several other officials over [[structural encroachment]] in the [[Red Sea Project]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-08/21/c_139307841.htm (Xinhua)]
*American actress [[Lori Loughlin]] is sentenced to two months in prison and her husband, fashion designer [[Mossimo Giannulli]], is sentenced to five months in prison for their role in the [[2019 college admissions bribery scandal|college admissions scandal]]. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-08-21/lori-loughlin-mossimo-giannulli-college-admissions-scandal-sentencing (''Los Angeles Times'')]
*Former California police officer [[Joseph James DeAngelo]], also known as the Golden State Killer, receives multiple consecutive life sentences without parole in the [[Superior Court of California of the County of Sacramento|county superior court]] in [[Sacramento]]. DeAngelo pleaded guilty in June to 13 counts of first-degree murder in exchange for taking the death penalty off the table. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/living-witness-teen-dads-murder-confronts-golden-state/story?id=72473195 (ABC News)]
*The press office of deposed [[President of Bolivia|Bolivian President]] [[Evo Morales]] rejects a criminal complaint filed this week by the Ministry of Justice accusing him of trafficking and raping a 16-year-old girl, claiming it was part of a "dirty war" waged by the interim government. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-morales-complaint/morales-office-denounces-sex-complaint-as-dirty-war-by-interim-government-idUSKBN25I0P1?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
***[[Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine|Irish Agriculture Minister]] [[Dara Calleary]] resigns after attending a golf dinner with more than 80 people, which came a day after Dublin announced a tightening of lockdown restrictions. [[Garda Síochána|Gardaí]] are now investigating possible breaches of COVID-19 regulations on the event. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53859988 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]], [[protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[Kenya Police|Police]] arrest anti-[[Corruption in Kenya|corruption]] protesters in [[Nairobi]] for allegedly disobeying [[Social distancing measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic|social distancing measures]]. Protesters, however, claim the arrests were an attempt by authorities to silence dissent and report that police have used [[tear gas]] to disperse the crowds. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/kenyan-police-teargas-anti-corruption-protesters-in-nairobi/2020/08/21/bb4cd452-e3ab-11ea-82d8-5e55d47e90ca_story.html (AP via ''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2019–2020 Iraqi protests]]
**Protesters in the southern city of [[Basra]] set fire to a local [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|parliament]] office after gathering to demand the resignation of governor [[Asaad Al Eidani]] for the killing of two activists last week. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/protesters-set-fire-to-parliament-office-in-iraqs-basra-idUSKBN25H2EG?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Doctors treating [[Russia]]n anti-[[corruption in Russia|corruption]] activist and opposition leader [[Alexei Navalny]] in [[Omsk]] refute claims that Navalny was poisoned before his flight from [[Tomsk]] to [[Moscow]] the previous day, citing that tests had shown no trace of any poison in his body. [[Chancellor of Germany|German Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] has offered to transfer Navalny to [[Berlin]] for further treatment by sending an [[air ambulance]] to Omsk, but doctors have refused to discharge him, saying Navalny is in an "unstable" condition. Navalny's spokeswoman Kira Yarmysh claim the refusal is a ploy to hide the poisoning and "put his life at risk". [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/russian-opposition-leader-poisned-no-trace-of-poison-found-in-navalny-tests-says-doctor-2283059 (AFP via NDTV)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2020 Kentucky Derby]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Kentucky]]
***[[Churchill Downs]] announces that the upcoming [[2020 Kentucky Derby|146th]] [[Kentucky Derby]] will run without fans due to [[COVID-19]] concerns including a rise in cases including in [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville]], [[Kentucky]]. [https://www.cbssports.com/general/news/2020-kentucky-derby-churchill-downs-announces-no-fans-will-attend-the-race-due-to-coronavirus-concerns/ (CBS Sports)] [https://www.courier-journal.com/story/entertainment/events/kentucky-derby/2020/08/21/churchill-downs-says-no-fans-at-kentucky-derby/5617467002/ (''Courier Journal'')]
*[[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]]
**In [[association football]], [[Sevilla FC]] defeat [[Inter Milan]] 3–2 in the [[2020 UEFA Europa League Final|final]] to win the [[UEFA Europa League]] for a record sixth time. [https://journalstar.com/sports/sevilla-beats-inter-milan-3-2-to-win-6th-europa-league/article_fa248a4b-c952-56b0-9388-60f2732b52dd.html (AP via ''Lincoln Journal Star'')]
